reference_document: Kasei 15 airframe, an OUT-OF-SAMPLE check: nothing in the airframe or the propeller is fitted to it. IJN test results (試験成績) of G4M1 aircraft No. 241 (Kasei 15, collector (non-thrust) exhausts, no wing-underside protection, Hamilton propellers; listed as Model 13, a designation Kasei 15 aircraft only received later) at the 9,500 kg reconnaissance-normal weight, as tabulated by WarbirdPerformanceBlog (warbirdperformance.livedoor.blog/archives/6848816.html; the original report was not read): 234.5 kt at 3,100 m and 244.0 kt at 5,900 m (true airspeed); 3,000 m in 5 min 27 s, 8,000 m in 20 min 18 s; service ceiling 9,660 m in 40 min 32 s. Power: Kasei 15 rated 2,350 rpm / +180 mmHg = 37.0 inHg (Navy engine manual; TAIC Manual No. 1 p.862). Flown with the Kasei 11 card's ASSUMED climb procedure unchanged (brake-release clock, 146 KCAS falling 0.6 kt per 1,000 ft, 112 KCAS ceiling climb) and the airframe drag fitted to aircraft No. 1. VALIDATION STATUS: fails climb above ~6,000 m vs aircraft No. 241: level speeds at 3,100 and 5,900 m pass out of sample (-0.5, +4.2 kt); time to 8,000 m is 10 % short, 8,000 m to the ceiling 57 % short, and the model still climbs 410 ft/min at No. 241's 9,660 m ceiling; time to 3,000 m is 5.5 % long. Cause not resolved on sourced data: the sourced ratings (1,280 hp at 6,000 m against the Kasei 11's 1,360 hp at 4,100 m) give the Kasei 15 about 16-25 % more power at 9.5 km on any density lapse, yet No. 241 reached only 140 m more ceiling than No. 1. Candidates without a source to decide them: No. 241's actual weight or drag (a prototype), the climb procedure, a Kasei 11 lapse error absorbed by the fitted span efficiency, and propeller losses at high altitude.
